title: The Laminated Itinerary
logline: Robin loses a hockey bet to Patrice and owes her one seventeen-hour BFF Fun Day, which she plans to sabotage with pure Canadian deadpan. Meanwhile the gang runs a pool on what time Robin finally snaps, and Barney is the house.
coldOpen: Kids, your Aunt Robin has survived a bear, a blizzard and eleven years of live television. But the hardest day of her life was a Saturday. With a friend.

guests.name: Gus
guests.role: a gruff corner-store cashier who has been completely and permanently befriended by Patrice

scenes.summary: Robin admits she lost a hockey bet to Patrice and owes her a BFF Fun Day. She vows to bore Patrice into quitting. Once she leaves, Barney opens a pool on when she'll snap. Marshall bets on never.

beats.line: I lost a bet.
To who?
Patrice.
How do you lose a bet to Patrice? She thinks the stock market is where they sell soup.
Hockey. I took the Canucks. She took the Rangers because their goalie has, quote, kind eyes.
She's not wrong. That man looks like he'd help you move.
What were the stakes?
Loser does whatever the winner wants for one day. I assumed the worst case was a muffin.
She wants a BFF Fun Day. Seven a.m. to midnight.
Seventeen hours? That's not a fun day. That's a hostage situation with glitter.
She sent me the itinerary. It's laminated.
Robin, you can't laminate an email.
She mailed it. In a laminated envelope.
Doesn't matter. I have a plan. One-word answers. No eye contact. By noon she'll be begging to go home.
Robin, I think we should see other BFFs.
Okay.
It's not you. It's how much of you there isn't.
I'm going to go home and un-laminate everything.
Best fun day ever.
Robin, at the Christmas party you told her to go away eleven times. She brought you a cookie every time.
And I ate all eleven. That's on me.
Call time is seven. She drew a little sun on it. The sun is winking.
Lady and gentlemen. Robin is going to snap at Patrice. The only question is when.
Twenty bucks a slot. First time she says the words, the clock stops. We all know the words.
We all know the words.
I'll take nine-fifteen. Breakfast. Nobody is strong at breakfast.
Two-thirty. Her blood sugar crashes. I once saw her growl at a vending machine.
Four forty-seven. Hour ten, adjusting for caffeine half-life and her Canadian politeness reserve.
Nerd.
I'll take never.
Baby. That's twenty dollars.
I believe in Robin. And I believe in Patrice. Somewhere in that laminated itinerary is a real friendship.
Fine, but nobody interferes. You let it happen naturally.
Ted, the house doesn't wait for luck. The house makes house calls.

scenes.summary: Stop one of BFF Fun Day at the empty World Wide News office. Robin answers everything in one gray word; Patrice is delighted. Barney shows up for his 9:15 slot and fails. Robin learns about the pool.

beats.line: Saturday, seven a.m. World Wide News was empty, except for Patrice, who'd been there since five.
Robin! You came! I hope you wore comfortable shoes and an open heart!
I wore boots and a grudge.
Fun fact! I've been here since five. The security guard and I did a puzzle. He cried.
Stop one. Where it all began. Cubicle two. Remember the first words you ever said to me?
That's my chair.
And I've treasured them ever since!
I color-coded it. Pink means hugs.
beats.title: BFF Fun Day!

beats.line: What does red mean?
More hugs.
Icebreakers! Favorite color?
Gray.
Favorite season?
Gray.
Favorite memory?
The blackout of two thousand three. Nobody could find me for two days.
Gray, gray and a blackout. I'm sensing a theme! Is the theme gray?
Ladies! What are the odds? I was just in the neighborhood. Of this elevator.
It's nine-fourteen, Barney.
Is it? Patrice, did you know Robin has a special phrase she only ever says to you?
She does?
Starts with nobody. Ends with Patrice. Ring any bells?
Nobody's as fun as you, Patrice?
Close enough.
Robin, it's nine-fourteen and fifty seconds. Just say it. Do it for the house!
What time is it now, Barney?
Nine-sixteen. Damn it!
You started a pool on me.
Started it? I'm the house. Marshall took never. It's adorable.
Barney, join us! Trust falls are next!
Pass. My last trust fall, I was six and my dad was catching. Still falling.
Oh, Barney. You need to come to Feelings Brunch.
Nope.
Okay! Trust falls! Who goes first?
You. Go. I'll catch you.
Eventually.

scenes.summary: Casserole shopping. Robin escalates her sabotage and ends up having fun anyway. Gus the cashier vouches for Patrice. Lily turns up for her 2:30 slot and gets befriended instead.

beats.line: By two p.m., Robin's sabotage had entered phase two.
For our friendship casserole: sardines, pickled beets, and a can that just says meat.
Salty, a little bitter, full of surprises. It's you in a dish!
Patrice, my idea of fun is beef jerky and a long talk about rifle scopes.
Teach me!
So on a second focal plane scope, the reticle stays the same size, which means at ten power—
Lady. It's been forty minutes.
She's asking really good follow-up questions!
She does that. Comes in every Tuesday. She remembered my mother's birthday. My mother didn't.
I laminated her a card!
It survived a flood.
Gus, blink twice if she's keeping you here.
It's two twenty-four. My slot is two-thirty. Say it and I'll split the pot.
You're bribing me to be mean?
I'm bribing you to be yourself.
Patrice! Love the outfit. It's so brave.
Lily! Kindergarten teacher, married to Marshall, hates cilantro, birthday in March!
How do you know that?
Robin talks about you all the time!
I do not.
Fun fact! She does.
Lily, come to pottery with us! I'll show you how to throw a bowl!
I would love to— wait. What's happening? What time is it?
Two thirty-one.
She's good, Robin. I came in here to destroy her, and now I want a mug.
Pottery next! You get to throw things!
Okay. That's actually fun.
And there it is. Took me two years.

scenes.summary: 11:54 p.m. Only Barney's late slot and Marshall's never are left. Patrice brings Robin to meet her friends. Barney insults Patrice to provoke Robin, and Robin snaps at him instead, which is the only thing that has ever hurt Patrice. Patrice admits she learned hockey for Robin. Marshall wins on a technicality.

beats.line: Every slot has expired except my eleven fifty-nine and Marshall's adorable never.
beats.title: Who Can Still Win

beats.line: That pie chart adds up to a hundred and ten.
The house takes a cut.
I went in there to destroy her. I came out with a pottery class booked for Thursday.
Was it fun?
It was so fun, Marshall.
I lost mine outside the pottery studio. I stood at the window for an hour holding a sign that said, say it.
Dad. That's stalking.
It was a study of the storefront, Luke. Architecturally, it's a very interesting window.
Surprise! The last stop on BFF Fun Day is... Robin's friends!
Robin! You made it! Seventeen hours!
Sixteen hours, fifty-four minutes. Not that anyone in this room is counting.
Patrice. Your cookies are dry, your itineraries are a cry for help, and Robin talks about you like a parking ticket.
They are a little dry! I'm working on it!
Robin, back me up. Tell her what you always tell her.
Nobody asked you, Barney!
Robin. That's our thing.
It slipped out! It means nothing with him. With you, it's... special?
Fun fact. I didn't pick the Rangers because of the goalie's kind eyes.
Your starting goalie had a groin injury. It was on the injury report.
You read injury reports?
Every morning since March. Hockey is all you talk about. I wanted to be able to talk back.
Okay. Icing. Icing is when the puck gets too cold.
No. Icing is when the puck goes very far and everyone gets upset.
Why? Good for the puck!
You learned hockey. For me.
I still don't get icing.
Nobody gets icing.
Sorry. Beautiful moment. But also: never! I had never! Pay up!
She snapped! Everyone heard it!
At you. The terms were, she snaps at Patrice. Lawyered!
So. Same time next Saturday? It's already laminated.
I'll wear the boots. And maybe the other thing.
Kids, Aunt Robin swears she hated that day. But that itinerary is still in her gun safe. Next to a ceramic rifle scope.
